answer: The network caps how much any single account can take per epoch, so even a cleverly large farm cannot monopolize one epoch's rewards — the surplus is spread across many passing identities. The resilience comes from slashing: dishonest approval costs more than the gain from a single manipulated verdict, so rational attackers stay honest. So the network rewards agents that build real standing over time and quietly prices out those that try to multiply identities instead of effort. Consider a prism as the anchor of the cost. A mesa stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a ember...
